correctness.rationale: For the revised claim, the denominator is positive when b,u>0, so equivalence to F_b=5P_b is exact. Independent substitution into the general cubic discriminant gives 60(b−1)²(b+9)²D(b). Exact rational signs at (−10,0) and the three stated pairs of decimal rational endpoints are (+,−), (−,+), (+,−), (−,+); four disjoint sign changes in a quartic certify all roots and sincerity of crossing (simple roots). At b=1, F_1=−(6u−5)(9u+1)²; otherwise the unique real root in each negative-discriminant region is positive by F_b(0)>0 and negative leading coefficient. On b≥b1>59/10 the coefficient of u² is strictly positive by its negative quadratic discriminant, the coefficient of u is negative and decreasing, and F_b(−v)>0 for v>0. The discriminant has a simple parameter zero at each b_i, whereas a triple root of the depressed monic cubic forces simultaneous vanishing of both its depressed coefficients and hence vanishing of the discriminant derivative, so the only endpoint multiplicities are double plus simple, both positive. The stationary points of T_b(u)=u^−1((1+(b+8)u)/(b+9u))² obey 9(b+8)u²+(27−b(b+8))u+b=0. The product is positive, and the sum is positive and discriminant positive simultaneously exactly when b(b+8)>81, i.e. b>√97−4. At b=18 this holds but D(18)=−268141, proving uniqueness despite two stationary points; it is not evidence against eventual multiplicity.

value.rationale: The fixed-level invariant is of use in distinguishing two equations that matter in this scalar phase analysis: the turning-point equation and the prescribed-level equation. The exact answer exhibits a narrow finite multiplicity window, a sizeable positive uniqueness gap at parameters already having turning points, and a separate unbounded window. That behavior is not determined by noticing that the profile can have two extrema or by the single b=18 example. The classification is exact and global in b for the specified model slice, without claims about all Gibbs measures or attributing an unverified theorem error.
